Design a simple NVMe controller state machine that handles three states: IDLE, READ, and WRITE. The controller should transition between these states based on a 2-bit input signal (`ctrl`). The signal `ctrl` defines the following operations:

01 - READ, 
10 - WRITE, 
11 - RETURN TO IDLE.

module nvme_controller (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [1:0] ctrl,
    output reg [1:0] state
);
    // State encoding
    localparam IDLE  = 2'b00;
    localparam READ  = 2'b01;
    localparam WRITE = 2'b10;

    // State transition
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE; // Reset to IDLE state
        end else begin
            case (ctrl)
                2'b00: state <= IDLE;   // Stay in IDLE
                2'b01: state <= READ;   // Transition to READ
                2'b10: state <= WRITE;  // Transition to WRITE
                2'b11: state <= IDLE;   // Return to IDLE
                default: state <= IDLE;  // Default to IDLE
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

The divider should operate in a clocked manner, utilizing a state machine to perform the division, restoring the dividend as needed.
code:
module restoring_divider(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [3:0] A,  // Dividend
    input [3:0] B,  // Divisor
    output reg [3:0] Q,  // Quotient
    output reg [3:0] R   // Remainder
);
    reg [4:0] R_temp;  // Temporary remainder (5 bits)
    reg [3:0] A_temp;  // Temporary dividend
    reg [2:0] count;   // Count for iteration
    reg [1:0] state;   // State variable
    localparam IDLE = 2'b00, DIVIDE = 2'b01, RESTORE = 2'b10, DONE = 2'b11;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            Q <= 4'b0000;
            R <= 4'b0000;
            R_temp <= 5'b00000;
            A_temp <= A;
            count <= 3'b000;
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (A_temp >= B) begin
                        R_temp <= {1'b0, A_temp}; // Start with A
                        Q <= 4'b0001; // First bit of quotient
                        A_temp <= A_temp - B; // Subtract B from A
                        state <= DIVIDE;
                    end else begin
                        Q <= 4'b0000;
                        R <= A_temp; // Remainder is A
                        state <= DONE;
                    end
                end
                DIVIDE: begin
                    if (count < 4) begin
                        R_temp <= {R_temp[3:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                        R_temp[0] <= A_temp[3]; // Lower bit of A
                        A_temp <= {A_temp[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift A
                        if (R_temp >= {1'b0, B}) begin
                            R_temp <= R_temp - {1'b0, B}; // Subtract B
                            Q <= {Q[2:0], 1'b1}; // Append 1 to quotient
                        end else begin
                            Q <= {Q[2:0], 1'b0}; // Append 0 to quotient
                        end
                        count <= count + 1;
                    end else begin
                        R <= R_temp[3:0]; // Set remainder
                        state <= DONE;
                    end
                end
                DONE: begin
                    // Stay in DONE state
                    // Optionally use this state to indicate completion
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an NVMe controller state machine that processes commands. The state machine should have the following states: IDLE, COMMAND_RECEIVED, PROCESSING, and COMPLETED. The state transitions should be triggered by the following signals: a command received signal (`cmd_rdy`), and a processing done signal (`proc_done`). The controller should output a status signal indicating the current state.
code:
module nvme_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input cmd_rdy,
    input proc_done,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: COMMAND_RECEIVED, 10: PROCESSING, 11: COMPLETED
);
    // State encoding
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00,
              COMMAND_RECEIVED = 2'b01,
              PROCESSING = 2'b10,
              COMPLETED = 2'b11;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (cmd_rdy) begin
                        state <= COMMAND_RECEIVED;
                    end
                end
                COMMAND_RECEIVED: begin
                    state <= PROCESSING;
                end
                PROCESSING: begin
                    if (proc_done) begin
                        state <= COMPLETED;
                    end
                end
                COMPLETED: begin
                    state <= IDLE; // Reset to IDLE after completing
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module serializer (

    input wire reset,
    input wire valid,
    input wire [15:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            bit_count <= 0;
            serial_out <= 0;
        end else if (valid) begin
            if (bit_count < 16) begin
                serial_out <= parallel_in[15 - bit_count]; // Send MSB first

            end else begin
                bit_count <= 0; // Reset after sending all bits

        end
    end

description:

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a simple state machine with three states (IDLE, PROCESS, DONE). The state machine transitions based on an input signal 'start'. Design a 16-bit serializer that converts a 16-bit parallel input into a serial output, sending one bit per clock cycle. );

K-means clustering assignment based on the minimum distance to cluster centroids.

The controller should have three states: HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW, represented by a 2-bit state variable. The output should represent the current frequency and voltage settings.

module DVFS_Controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] temperature, // 8-bit temperature input
    output reg [1:0] state, // 2-bit state output
    output reg [1:0] voltage, // 2-bit voltage level
    output reg [1:0] frequency // 2-bit frequency level
);

    localparam MEDIUM = 2'b01;
    localparam LOW = 2'b10;

        if (reset) begin
            state <= MEDIUM; // Default state
            voltage <= 2'b10; // Default high voltage
            frequency <= 2'b10; // Default high frequency
        end else begin
            case (state)
                HIGH: begin

    input wire send,      // Signal to send data
    input wire [7:0] data, // 8-bit data input
    output reg tx        // Transmit output
);

    reg [11:0] baud_count; // Baud rate counter

    parameter IDLE = 4'b0000, START_BIT = 4'b0001, DATA_BITS = 4'b0010, STOP_BIT = 4'b0011;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                tx <= 1; // Idle state, tx high
                if (send) begin
                    state <= START_BIT; // Move to start bit
                    bit_index <= 0; // Reset bit index
                    baud_count <= 0; // Reset baud count
                end
            end
            
            START_BIT: begin
                tx <= 0; // Start bit is low
                if (baud_count == 10416) begin // Wait for one bit duration (1 MHz clock for 9600 baud)
                    baud_count <= 0; // Reset baud count
                    state <= DATA_BITS; // Move to data bits
                end else begin
                    baud_count <= baud_count + 1; 
                end
            end
            
            DATA_BITS: begin
                tx <= data[bit_index]; // Transmit data bit
                if (baud_count == 10416) begin // Wait for one bit duration
                    baud_count <= 0; // Reset baud count
                    if (bit_index == 7) begin
                        state <= STOP_BIT; // Move to stop bit
                    end else begin
                        bit_index <= bit_index + 1; // Move to next bit
                    end
                end else begin
                    baud_count <= baud_count + 1; 
                end
            end

            STOP_BIT: begin
                tx <= 1; // Stop bit is high
                if (baud_count == 10416) begin // Wait for one bit duration
                    baud_count <= 0; // Reset baud count
                    state <= IDLE; // Back to idle
                end else begin
                    baud_count <= baud_count + 1; 
                end
            end

            default: state <= IDLE; // Default state
        endcase
    end
endmodule

    input wire rst,
    input wire [7:0] temperature,  // 8-bit temperature input
    output reg shutdown_signal       // output shutdown signal

    reg temp_exceeded; // Flag to indicate if temperature exceeds threshold

            count <= 0;
            temp_exceeded <= 0;

- From IDLE to WRITE on start signal
- From READ to IDLE on read complete signal
- From WRITE to IDLE on write complete signal
- Any state can transition to ERROR on error signal
The module should output the current state of the state machine.

    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire read_complete,
    input wire write_complete,
    input wire error,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: READ, 10: WRITE, 11: ERROR
);

    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, READ = 2'b01, WRITE = 2'b10, ERROR = 2'b11;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= (start && !read_complete) ? READ : WRITE;
                    end
                end
                READ: begin
                    if (read_complete) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end else if (error) begin
                        state <= ERROR;
                    end
                end
                WRITE: begin
                    if (write_complete) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end else if (error) begin
                        state <= ERROR;
                    end
                end
                ERROR: begin
                    if (reset) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
                default: state <= IDLE;
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

                if (dist[edges[j]] > dist[i] + weights[j]) begin

                        bit_index <= 0;

                    state <= DATA_BITS;
